parts.title: Library
parts.article:
(A) Libraries are collections of materials containing information, ideas, and works of imagination that are organized for public use and staffed by people trained to provide a service. They take many physical forms ranging from large purpose-built buildings to rooms in parent institutions and small temporary structures. They are a vital resource in an age in which people and communities desperately need to consider alternative points of view and information in order to challenge the mass media and make up their own minds.

(B) Despite a popular misconception, libraries have never confined themselves to the collection of books. Traditionally, they have acquired a range of print-based materials, including newspapers, maps, pamphlets, illustrations, and many other items. Indeed, libraries pre-dated the invention of the book. For example, the original library in Alexandria, the capital of ancient Egypt, collected papyrus scrolls, and mediaeval monasteries collected manuscripts. It was therefore widely regarded as a logical step for libraries to collect every new medium that contained information as it emerged. All forms of sound and visual recording (for example, gramophone records, cassettes, videos, CDs, and DVDs) joined the collections in many libraries as they became available. Digital formats were also quickly added to collections and there are now countless libraries around the world which have fully integrated electronic resources such as e-books, audiobooks, online databases, and digitised archives.

(C) However, the role of libraries has expanded beyond mere collection. Modern libraries also function as community hubs, offering public internet access, literacy programmes, and spaces for civic engagement. In many regions, libraries provide essential services such as assistance with job applications, legal guidance, and support for small businesses. Furthermore, librarians have adapted to the digital age by developing skills in data management, digital literacy training, and fact-checking – all of which help users navigate an increasingly complex information landscape.

(D) Nevertheless, libraries face significant challenges. Budget cuts in many countries have reduced opening hours and staff numbers. Some critics argue that physical libraries are obsolete, given that so much information is now available online. Yet proponents maintain that libraries offer something the internet cannot: curated, trustworthy information and equitable access regardless of income or social status. In conclusion, while the format of materials has evolved, the core mission of libraries – to provide free and open access to knowledge – remains as relevant today as it was in ancient Alexandria.
parts.questions:
Questions 14-18
Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 2?
In boxes 14-18 on your answer sheet, write.

Q14 Libraries have only existed since the invention of the printing press.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q15 The library in Alexandria collected papyrus scrolls rather than books.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q16 Modern librarians are trained to help users evaluate online information.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q17 All countries have increased their spending on public libraries.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q18 Libraries have never collected sound recordings such as cassettes or CDs.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN
Questions 19-22
Complete the sentences below.
Choose NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from the passage for each answer.
19 Libraries are described as a vital resource for people to challenge the .
20 In mediaeval times, monasteries collected instead of printed books.
21 Besides information storage, modern libraries function as .
22 Unlike the internet, libraries provide access regardless of a person's financial situation.
Questions 23–26
Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

Q23 According to the passage, libraries have traditionally collected:

  • A only books and manuscripts
  • B a wide variety of print-based items
  • C exclusively digital materials
  • D only sound recordings

Q24 What do critics of modern libraries argue?

  • A Libraries are too expensive to maintain.
  • B Information is mostly available online, making libraries unnecessary.
  • C Librarians lack proper training.
  • D Libraries should focus only on e-books.

Q25 Which of the following is mentioned as a service provided by modern libraries?

  • A Medical treatment
  • B Housing assistance
  • C Job application support
  • D Free meals

Q26 What is the author's conclusion about libraries today?

  • A They are no longer useful.
  • B Their main purpose has completely changed.
  • C Their fundamental mission remains the same despite changes in format.
  • D They should only exist in large cities.

reference:
Q14

解析 原文明确说图书馆的出现比书的发明还要早，所以题目说“只在印刷术后存在”是错的。

干扰 你可能会以为前一句提到的印刷品就是起点，但紧接着的原文直接推翻了这点。

句子 Despite a popular misconception, libraries have never confined themselves to the collection of books. Traditionally, they have acquired a range of print-based materials, including newspapers, maps, pamphlets, illustrations, and many other items. Indeed, libraries pre-dated the invention of the book.

Q15

解析 原文举例明确提到，亚历山大图书馆收集的是纸莎草卷轴（papyrus scrolls）。

干扰 原文明确指出图书馆的历史“早于书籍的发明（pre-dated the invention of the book）”。

句子 Indeed, libraries pre-dated the invention of the book. For example, the original library in Alexandria, the capital of ancient Egypt, collected papyrus scrolls, and mediaeval monasteries collected manuscripts.

Q16

解析 原文说图书管理员发展了数字素养培训和事实核查技能，帮助用户在复杂的信息环境中导航，也就是对应题目说的评估在线信息。

干扰 你可能会觉得“navigate”和“evaluate”字面不同，但“fact-checking”本身就是评估信息真假的过程。

句子 Furthermore, librarians have adapted to the digital age by developing skills in data management, digital literacy training, and fact-checking – all of which help users navigate an increasingly complex information landscape.

Q17

解析 原文明确说许多国家削减了预算（Budget cuts），这和题目里说的“所有国家都增加了花费”完全相反。

干扰 你看到“many countries”可能会犹豫是不是全集，但这道题直接错在“削减”和“增加”的动作相反上。

句子 Nevertheless, libraries face significant challenges. Budget cuts in many countries have reduced opening hours and staff numbers.

Q18

解析 原文清楚写明了磁带、CD等各种形式的声音和视觉记录都被加入了图书馆的收藏中。

干扰 题目加了“never”（从不）这个绝对词，遇到这种词一定要回到原文看是否有具体例子反驳。

句子 It was therefore widely regarded as a logical step for libraries to collect every new medium that contained information as it emerged. All forms of sound and visual recording (for example, gramophone records, cassettes, videos, CDs, and DVDs) joined the collections in many libraries as they became available.

Q19

解析 原文直接提到了人们需要去挑战大众传媒（challenge the mass media），把 mass media 填进去刚好符合。

干扰 不要填成前面的 points of view，因为题目要求的是去“challenge（挑战）”什么对象。

句子 They are a vital resource in an age in which people and communities desperately need to consider alternative points of view and information in order to challenge the mass media and make up their own minds.

Q20

解析 原文直接指出中世纪的修道院（mediaeval monasteries）收集的是手稿（manuscripts）。

干扰 你可能会误填成同一句里的 papyrus scrolls，但那是亚历山大图书馆收集的，看清主语是修道院。

句子 Indeed, libraries pre-dated the invention of the book. For example, the original library in Alexandria, the capital of ancient Egypt, collected papyrus scrolls, and mediaeval monasteries collected manuscripts.

Q21

解析 原文提到图书馆的角色已经超出了单纯的收集，现代图书馆还可以作为社区中心（community hubs）来发挥作用。

干扰 不要填后面的 public internet access，因为 function as 后面需要跟身份或角色，而不是具体的服务项目。

句子 However, the role of libraries has expanded beyond mere collection. Modern libraries also function as community hubs, offering public internet access, literacy programmes, and spaces for civic engagement.

Q22

解析 原文说图书馆提供互联网不能提供的公平访问（equitable access），不考虑收入或社会地位，恰好对应题目的“不管个人的财务状况”。

干扰 你可能会被前面的 trustworthy information 吸引，但填空处紧跟着 access，修饰 access 的词只有 equitable。

句子 Some critics argue that physical libraries are obsolete, given that so much information is now available online. Yet proponents maintain that libraries offer something the internet cannot: curated, trustworthy information and equitable access regardless of income or social status.

Q23

解析 原文提到传统上它们获取的是“一系列基于印刷的材料（a range of print-based materials）”，这直接对应选项B的内容。

干扰 你可能会选A，但原文明确说了不仅限于书籍，还包含报纸、地图等各种资料。

句子 Despite a popular misconception, libraries have never confined themselves to the collection of books. Traditionally, they have acquired a range of print-based materials, including newspapers, maps, pamphlets, illustrations, and many other items.

Q24

解析 原文提到批评者认为实体图书馆已经过时了，因为现在有太多的信息可以在线获取，直接对应B选项。

干扰 你可能会选A，原文前面虽然提到了预算削减（budget cuts），但这并不是“批评者（critics）”论证图书馆没用的理由。

句子 Some critics argue that physical libraries are obsolete, given that so much information is now available online.

Q25

解析 原文在列举图书馆提供的服务时，清楚地提到了“协助求职申请（assistance with job applications）”，对应C选项。

干扰 这题属于细节寻找，医疗、住房或免费餐食在原文中根本没有出现过，不要自己脑补。

句子 In many regions, libraries provide essential services such as assistance with job applications, legal guidance, and support for small businesses.

Q26

解析 文章最后的结论句说，尽管材料格式演变了，但图书馆的核心使命仍然像古代一样有现实意义，直接对应C选项的使命不变。

干扰 你可能会选B，但原文说的是材料格式变了（format of materials has evolved），而不是它的主要目的完全变了。

句子 In conclusion, while the format of materials has evolved, the core mission of libraries – to provide free and open access to knowledge – remains as relevant today as it was in ancient Alexandria.
